parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ankërijas, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *angurjás. Cognate to Lithuanian ungurys, Old Prussian angurgis and Finnish ankerias.
From Proto-Finnic *herhiläinen, from an earlier *šerši + *-läinen, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *śirˀšṓ, compare Lithuanian širšė, Finnish herhiläinen (“wasp”).
From Proto-Finnic *këplas, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Latvian kaplis, Lithuanian kaplys).

parole.significato: straw, culm; stem, stalk (of a grassy plant)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *korci, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *karti (compare Lithuanian kartis (“bar, thin rod”)). Cognate with Finnish korsi, Votic kõrsi, Karelian korsi and Veps korz.

From Proto-Finnic *koukkoi, probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic *kaukas. Compare Lithuanian kaukas (“ghost”) and Old Prussian cawx (“devil”). Cognate to dialectal/archaic Finnish kouko (“ghost, death”).

From Proto-Finnic *leinä, possibly from Proto-Baltic [Term?], compare Lithuanian klienas (“thin, skinny”) and Latvian kliens (“thin, withered”). Cognate to Votic leine (“grief”), Ingrian leina (“sadness”), and Finnish leina (“poor, weak, a poor crop yield”).

parole.significato: broom, besom (a sweeping tool made of twigs)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *luuta, ultimately from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare modern Latvian slota and Lithuanian šluota). Cognates include Finnish luuta, Livonian lūdõ, Votic lootõ, luutõ, Ingrian luuta, Ludian luud and Veps lud.
From Proto-Finnic *oka, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic. Cognates include Finnish oas, oka (dialectal), Votic õgaz, Ingrian oas, Livvi ovas, Ludian ogas and Veps ogah.

From Proto-Finnic *pëtra (“deer; reindeer”), probably from Proto-Baltic. Cognates include Finnish peura (“wild reindeer”), Votic põdra, Livonian põ’ddõr(z), Livvi pedru, Ludian and Veps pedr (“deer”).

From Proto-Finnic *rühmä (compare Finnish ryhmä), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian trūkšmas). Originally a dialectal word, brought into the standard language by example of Finnish.

From Proto-Finnic *sapa, from Proto-Baltic *stabara-, compare Lithuanian stabaras (“dried branch”) and Latvian stebere (“cow's tail”). Cognate to Finnish saparo, Ingrian sapara (“pig's tail”), and Karelian sapero, saparo (“tail”).

From Proto-Finnic *takijas, ultimately from Proto-Baltic *dagijas (“burdock”) (compare modern Latvian dadzis and Lithuanian dagys). Cognate with Finnish takiainen, Votic and Ingrian takkiain, Ludian takkiaińe, Livvi takkis- (in the compound takkisheinü (“burdock”)) and Veps takkiž. The word has folk

parole.significato: bee (gathering for carrying out a major task, such as harvesting or construction), dugnad
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *talko- (compare Finnish talkoot, Karelian talloh, Veps touguh, Votic talko), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian talka (“cooperated voluntary work”)).
From Proto-Finnic *taibas, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *staipas. Cognate with Finnish seiväs. The *s ~ *t variation may be due to the initial *st- in the Baltic etymon.
From Proto-Finnic *togëh, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *takis.
Inherited from Proto-Finnic *torvi, from earlier *towri, from Proto-Baltic, from Proto-Indo-European *táwros. Compare Finnish torvi, Karelian torvi, Veps torv.
From Proto-Finnic *upa, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (Latvian pupa). Cognate with Livonian pubā.

parole.significato: an apple (a common, round fruit produced by the tree Malus domestica, cultivated in temperate climates.)
parole.testo: A South Estonian dialectal word, probably derived from uba (“bean”), from Proto-Finnic *upa, from Proto-Baltic [Term?]. Original sense likely "small and round object".

From Proto-Finnic *vaidëldak, from Proto-Baltic. Irregular stem vaiel- in forms like the da-infinitive result from regular phonological developments: *vaitelema → *vaitlema → vaidlema, but *vaiðelðak → vaielda (-da is an analogical form). Derived from Proto-Finnic *varas, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *vāras, compare Lithuanian voras (“old”). Cognate to Finnish varhain.

parole.significato: phase, stage, round, e.g. in a competition
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vooro, possibly a loan from Proto-Baltic [Term?], compare Lithuanian vora (“line, row”).
From Proto-Finnic *vähi, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Latvian vēzis and Lithuanian vėžys).

From Proto-Finnic *häici, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?]. Compare Lithuanian žiedas and Latvian zieds. Cognate with Finnish hede, hedelmä, Veps heiditä (“to blossom”), and Votic edʹdʹittsä (“to blossom (mainly used for rye)”).
